html:
Papa Wemba was a Congolese singer, one of the most famous stars of African music, known for his high voice and his style.

He was a founder of the band Zaiko Langa Langa in 1969, which brought a youthful, faster sound to Congolese rumba, and then led Viva La Musica from 1977. He moved between Kinshasa and Paris and won fans in Europe through the world music scene.

He was the leading figure of la sape, the cult of elegant designer clothes among young men of the two Congos. He died after collapsing on stage at a festival in Abidjan in April 2016, and was mourned with a national funeral in Kinshasa.
